title: Cross Lake Atitlan between the villages
description: A caldera lake ringed by three volcanoes and a dozen Maya villages, each with its own dialect and dress, connected only by boat.

title: Watch sunrise over the canopy from Temple IV at Tikal
description: Maya temples pushing up through rainforest, with howler monkeys roaring in the dark before dawn. The view from Temple IV was used as a rebel base in Star Wars.

title: Watch Semana Santa carpets in Antigua
description: Coloured sawdust laid into elaborate street carpets overnight, then destroyed by the procession walking over them at dawn.

title: Climb Acatenango to watch Fuego erupt
description: An overnight climb to 3,976m to camp opposite an active volcano that erupts every twenty minutes through the night. Cold, steep and unforgettable.

title: Swim the limestone pools at Semuc Champey
description: A natural limestone bridge carrying turquoise pools over a river that runs underneath it. The road in is genuinely rough and takes hours.

title: Dive the Great Blue Hole
description: A 318m-wide collapsed cave system 124m deep, with stalactites at 40m proving it was dry land during the last ice age. Advanced certification required.

title: Snorkel with rays at Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley
description: A cut through the Belize Barrier Reef - the largest in the northern hemisphere - where nurse sharks and southern stingrays gather in waist-deep water.

title: Wade into the ATM cave at Actun Tunichil Muknal
description: You swim into a cave to reach Maya sacrificial remains calcified into the floor, including the Crystal Maiden. Cameras have been banned since one was dropped on a skull.

title: Soak in the hot springs under Arenal
description: A near-perfect cone that erupted continuously from 1968 until 2010 and is now dormant. The river running off it is naturally heated to bath temperature.

title: Walk the hanging bridges in the Monteverde cloud forest
description: Founded by Quaker pacifists who left the US in 1951. Resplendent quetzals nest here, and the forest is permanently inside the cloud layer.

title: Look for tapirs in Corcovado
description: National Geographic called it the most biologically intense place on earth - all four Costa Rican monkey species, plus tapir, jaguar and scarlet macaw.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Tortuguero
description: The most important green turtle nesting site in the western Caribbean, reachable only by boat or small plane through a network of jungle canals.

title: Zip-line through the Guanacaste canopy
description: Canopy zip-lining was invented in Costa Rica in the 1970s as a way for biologists to study the treetops, and became an industry by accident.

title: Watch a ship transit the Panama Canal locks
description: Around 14,000 ships a year lifted 26m over the isthmus by gravity-fed locks. The Miraflores visitor centre puts you level with the deck of a passing vessel.

title: Sail the San Blas islands with the Guna
description: 365 islands governed autonomously by the Guna, who set their own visitor rules and sell molas - reverse-applique panels sewn by hand.

title: Find the red frogs on Isla Bastimentos
description: Strawberry poison dart frogs that vary in colour island to island - a textbook case of populations diverging in isolation.

title: Volcano board down Cerro Negro
description: You walk up an active black cinder cone carrying a plywood board, then sit on it and slide down the ash at up to 90km/h.

title: Cycle between the two volcanoes of Ometepe
description: An hourglass island formed by two volcanoes rising out of a freshwater lake, with pre-Columbian petroglyphs on the lower slopes.

title: Look into the lava lake at Masaya
description: One of very few volcanoes on earth where you can drive to the rim and look directly down at moving lava. Visits are timed and short for good reason.

title: Learn to dive on Utila
description: Among the cheapest places in the world to get certified, on the Mesoamerican Reef, with whale sharks passing through much of the year.

title: Read the hieroglyphic stairway at Copan
description: 63 steps carrying around 2,200 glyphs - the longest Maya inscription known, and the finest stone carving anywhere in the Maya world.

title: Surf the point at El Tunco
description: Consistent right-hand point breaks over rock and black sand, on a coast that has quietly become one of Central America's best surf destinations.

title: Drive the Ruta de las Flores
description: 36km through coffee highlands and five colonial towns, with weekend food fairs and murals on nearly every wall in Ataco.
